cues: A perfect conductor is an imaginary material with zero resistance and nothing else.
Cool it in a magnetic field, and it traps whatever flux was inside, so its final state depends on its history.
A real superconductor expels the flux whichever order you do things in.
Its state is always the same: a true thermodynamic phase.

Its state is always the same: a true thermodynamic phase.
